I'm kind of curious. I understand wolfenstein style raycasting to a degree, but I can't wrap my head around 3d rendering. Nor can I find an easily understandable algorithim to look at and understand.
So how do modern 3d engines render things?

Do you mean a Game Engine or only the parts related to rendering, i.e the last few calls to OpenGL/DirectX/Mangle/etc.

A lot of people have a lot of ideas about what a 3D engine is exactly.
Only the parts related to rendering itself.

Well, on the software side you just copy over the vertices of the model and possibly the color of each vertex/faces/whatever. You might then copy over some textures and the mappings that go with them. Then there are the rotations you need to copy over as well.

Then you do your OpenGL render call (glDrawElements/whatever) or your DirectX render call (context->DrawIndexed/whatever) and you pretty much done. The GPU takes over after this point and runs through the graphics pipeline finally ending up at the rasterization. If you are looking for some type of algorithm or data-structure there isn't really one. They use arrays and have an algorithm in the big sense but nothing like ray tracing or heaps.

Sorry if this was not indepth enough or what you expected. To learn about the graphics pipeline there are resources online. You might be better asking this on a different subverse really.
